clue.text: Being filmed, one crossing river with artist

indicators.note: one word crossing another lies across it, so the first wraps around the second

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A painter is caught on film as someone wades across a river with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One crossing river' reads as a person wading, but the word one itself straddles the river's name. The Cam is the river through Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening on camera is being recorded by a film or television crew.

clue.text: King of Mercia removed from one

parts.note: a, as in a single one

explanation.surface: A Saxon king is deposed by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in the English Midlands; Offa built the dyke along the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa ruled the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia in the eighth century, a historical monarch.

clue.text: Witty type in vehicle, on top of double-decker

indicators.note: the top of a word written downward is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A joker travels in a car stacked on a two-storey bus.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, CAR sits 'on' D. A double-decker is a two-level British bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is old-fashioned slang for an amusing, eccentric person, a joker or wag.

clue.text: My flute made Bart adaptation of opera

indicators.note: an adaptation reworks material into a new form, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: Bart Simpson turns Puccini into a flute piece, courtesy of the speaker's instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame Butterfly is Puccini's well-known opera about a Japanese geisha and an American naval officer.

clue.text: Famous twin in rock band, American

parts.note: R.E.M. is an American rock band
US is short for the United States, American

explanation.surface: A well-known twin plays in an American rock group.
explanation.definitionFit: Remus and his brother Romulus were the legendary twin founders of Rome, suckled by a wolf.

clue.text: A male exercises, provides entertainment

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
exercises a right means uses it

explanation.surface: A man working out at the gym is a source of fun to onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercises' looks like gym work but means puts to use.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse is to entertain or divert someone, making them laugh or pass time pleasantly.

clue.text: Army officer in the car may tail it, surreptitiously

indicators.note: acting surreptitiously means moving in a hidden, roundabout way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy-thriller scene: a soldier is followed secretly by a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A military attaché is an army officer posted to an embassy abroad as a defence adviser.

clue.text: Mostly put on outrageous things for male-only dos

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the next word is dropped

parts.note: to stage a play is to put it on

indicators.note: something outrageous is wild and out of order, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Wild antics are laid on at parties for men only.
explanation.walkthrough: STAGE loses its last letter. A stag night is a groom's pre-wedding party with male friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Stag nights are celebrations held for a bridegroom with only his male friends present.

clue.text: Wise guy responsible for right yarn aboard fishing boat

indicators.note: cargo aboard a vessel sits inside it, so these words go within the boat

parts.note: a smack is a small sailing fishing vessel

explanation.surface: A know-all is to blame for some sailor's tall story on a trawler.
explanation.definitionFit: A wise guy and a smart aleck are both irritating know-alls, idiomatic synonyms.

clue.text: Gas lit by a member

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone ignites gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lit' could be read as literature, but here it means set burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is the explosive methane gas found in coal mines, a hazard to miners.

clue.text: A record, one about South American animal

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record
a, as in a single one
ca is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone sets a record with an exotic Andean beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a domesticated camelid from the Andes, kept for its fine wool.

clue.text: Leave with one cast in greatest part for screen

indicators.note: something cast in is thrown into another thing, so it ends up inside it

parts.note: the most is the greatest part

explanation.surface: An actor quits after being cast in a leading role for the big screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen' tempts as film, but it is a protective mesh.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosquito net is fine mesh hung around a bed to keep out biting insects, a kind of screen.

clue.text: One who should lead the way with that girl following us

definitions.text: One who should lead the way

indicators.note: following means coming behind, so the girl's word goes after the word placed next to it

explanation.surface: A guide arrives with a young woman walking behind the group.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher shows people to their seats in a church, theatre or cinema, guiding them along.

clue.text: Drive ahead of GP with spokesperson

parts.note: a spin is a short drive in a car
a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

explanation.surface: A motorist goes past the local surgery with a press officer.
explanation.walkthrough: A spin is British for a short pleasure drive, and GP (general practitioner) is the family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin doctor is a political press officer who presents news in a favourable light.

clue.text: Bad-tempered Latin ruled out

indicators.note: out here means disordered or wrong, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A grumpy classics master bans Latin from the curriculum.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-natured describes a surly, cross disposition, synonymous with grumpy or irritable.

clue.text: Cooked cheap lamb in Florida resort

indicators.note: food that is cooked is transformed, so these letters change their order

explanation.surface: A budget dinner of lamb is served on a Florida holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Palm Beach is a wealthy town on Florida's Atlantic coast, a famous holiday destination.

clue.text: Lost, sailing

definitions.meaning: second meaning: out on the ocean in a ship

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like a sailor gone astray; they are separate senses of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both bewildered and literally out on the ocean, away from land.

clue.text: Magnificent drink knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back suggests something pushed backwards, so the word is read from its end

explanation.surface: A splendid beer is downed in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' sounds like swallowing a drink, which is also its trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means kingly or stately, fit for royalty and so magnificent in appearance.

clue.text: Group of singers, not one with bit of talent

indicators.note: a bit of a word is just its first small piece

explanation.surface: A choir in which none of the members has any talent.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine musicians or singers, or a piece written for nine.

clue.text: Derisive, actors in dress costume at first

indicators.note: in means placed within, so one piece is wrapped by the garment

parts.note: a sari is an Indian woman's dress
the actors in a play are its cast

indicators.note: at first points to just the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A critic sneers at the players in their first costume fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcastic remarks mock or scorn someone through irony, the essence of being derisive.

clue.text: Working on article on eccentric, dying

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A journalist writes a piece about an odd character who is near death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' sounds like a newspaper piece; it is the grammatical word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the way out is declining or close to its end, idiomatically near death.

clue.text: Chancellor, at Exchequer, has to make a speech

indicators.note: has means contains, so the words before it hold the solution inside them

parts.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: The Chancellor of the Exchequer must address Parliament on the budget.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is Britain's finance minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal address, often in a pompous manner.

clue.text: Assist cub having lost leader

indicators.note: losing the leader means the front letter goes

parts.note: a whelp is a young animal, a cub

explanation.surface: Someone aids a young scout who has no pack leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To help someone is to assist them, a plain synonym for giving aid.

clue.text: Astonish group of teachers turning up after start of show

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter
in a down entry, turning up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers

explanation.surface: Teachers astonish everyone by arriving after the play has started.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to amaze or stupefy someone, leaving them shocked and speechless.

clue.text: Slight quarrel about a rate initially shown in a list of charges

indicators.note: about means around, so the quarrel surrounds what follows

parts.note: a tiff is a minor argument

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A minor row breaks out over the price quoted on a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a published schedule of prices or duties, such as hotel rates or customs fees.

clue.text: Cunning shown in one quarter where there's a fighting fund

indicators.note: shown in means displayed inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: west is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: Craftiness in one part of town where campaign money is raised.
explanation.definitionFit: A war chest is money set aside for a campaign or battle, a reserve for fighting.

clue.text: Type of overnight flight that provides cheap whisky?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a night flight that leaves passengers bleary
second meaning: American slang for rough, low-grade whisky

explanation.surface: A late-night plane where the bar serves rotgut.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-eye is a nickname for a night flight arriving early, and also old slang for raw whisky.

clue.text: Look closely taking in opening of test, and then criticise play

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing, so one word holds the other within it

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: critics pan a show they dislike

explanation.surface: A reviewer studies a test performance then slates the production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' as criticise is a familiar reviewing verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan is J. M. Barrie's play about the boy who never grows up.
